Subject: Renewal planning — capacity ask (8→16)

Hi Aditya,

Our renewal for Dedicated is coming up (early August) and we'd like to discuss bumping our reserved pool from 8 → 16 GPUs. We've had two models spike in usage and the current queueing is starting to affect latency-sensitive features for our insights product.

High level asks:
- Pricing delta for moving to 16 GPUs under a monthly commit (we currently have an 8-GPU monthly commit).
- Throughput / latency guardrails you can commit to (p50/p95/p99 for 512-token prompts).
- Options for a phased activation (we'd prefer a staged ramp over ~4 weeks).

Can we get a ballpark and schedule a 30-min call next week? If possible please include an ops contact for rollout details.

Thanks,
Peter
VP Product, Orchard Analytics

Hi Peter — thanks for the heads up and context. Happy to run through options. Quick summary from my side:

1) Pricing: moving from 8→16 GPUs we typically structure as an updated monthly commit with a 1.85x price multiplier on the current per-GPU rate (we can give an exact figure after I pull your current SKU). We'll also propose a 90-day phased billing option to smooth the delta.

2) SLOs: for 512-token workloads on our Dedicated tier we can offer: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 220ms when on the dedicated 16-GPU pool with appropriate instance types. For more aggressive p99 targets we recommend a small compute buffer (burst capacity) which I can price separately.

3) Activation: staged activation over 2–4 weeks is common: reserve the additional GPUs immediately for capacity planning, activate 8 more GPUs in week 1, traffic ramp week 2–4 with KV/prefix caching warmup. Ops will run pre-cutover checks and a traffic cutover window (we typically do a 2–hour window for production switch).

I attached a draft amendment (Redwood_Dedicated_Amendment_v2.pdf) and an ops checklist (stub) — want to get your legal/ops review and then we can DocuSign. Can you do Tuesday 6/29 10am PT for 30 minutes?

Adding ops/renewals detail from our side — putting a proposed terms bullet list here so Peter has a clear picture before the call: 

- Term: 12-month renewal, start date aligned with Orchard's renewal window (we'll pro-rate partial month).
- Monthly commit: increase to a 16-GPU-equivalent commitment; billing breaks down to a per-GPU unit price and token-based overages.
- Phased activation: Week 0: reservation and capacity prep; Week 1: +4 GPUs active for internal traffic; Week 2: +4 GPUs (total +8); Week 3: remaining +4 GPUs (total +12); Week 4: final +4 GPUs (total +16). We can compress to 2 weeks on request.
- Throughput guarantee: we propose an SLO of sustained 60 tokens/s per GPU for your family of models; this maps to approximately 960 tokens/s at 16 GPUs. For tail latency (p99) we include an ops-runbook and automatic fallback to the 8-GPU baseline if latency exceeds threshold during the ramp.
- Billing smoothing: offer a 3-month rate smoothing credit to avoid a large immediate invoice spike (applies against the first 3 monthly invoices).

Ops attachment: OPS_Rollout_Checklist.xlsx (staging/runbook/prod cutover steps). I'll be on the call Tuesday to go through the cutover milestones.

Marissa
